messages.content:
You finish a dry-stone wall. The wall is built course by course with Wang's method; you act only at the end, when every remaining stone is on offer. At each placement you choose which candidate to place: a stone in one of four rotations, at the position Wang's image convolution found for it. Every listed candidate is feasible (LLC > 0). Your goal is the finished wall, judged on four metrics: F_SF, stone filling (the share of the wall area that is stone, higher is better); F_AH, the horizontal joint path index (lower is better: no long continuous horizontal joints); F_AV, the vertical joint path index (higher is better: vertical joints are staggered); F_LR, the smaller of the left and right kinematic limit loads of the wall divided by the friction coefficient (higher is better). A stone that cannot be placed is lost to the wall.
Data. Stones are labelled S1, S2, ... in the order they were first sampled. Coordinates are pixels in the evaluation frame (mirrored when building from the right, so 'left' is the side the course is built from); rows count upward from the ground. Each candidate: id, stone, rotation, its pose x and y, the width and height of its bounding box, and Wang's five filter scores (higher is better for each): NHR course height (0 = level with its left neighbour), GDS global density, IWR interlocking (its vertical joint far from the joints below), LLC the kinematic limit load of the wall with the stone added and stabilized, divided by the friction coefficient, LFR local void (0 = flush on the left and on the bottom). wall summarizes the current wall; unplaceable lists stones on offer with no feasible candidate now. Nothing about the final wall is known.
Compare the main candidates on all five scores and on what they leave for the remaining stones; in the rationale state each one's main advantages and costs. Finish with commit_pick.

arguments.rationale:
Choose S14 at 180°: NHR -0.273, GDS 1.0, IWR 0.538, LLC 0.517 and LFR -0.0167. It combines the best local flushness with a wide, dense placement, good staggering and the highest offered load score. Its course height is less level than S16/0 or S7/180, and its width occupies much of the shared x≈237–329 opportunity. Using S14 now also avoids relying on its more void-prone upright alternatives.

S15/0 has slightly better IWR (0.556) but worse NHR (-0.319) and LFR (-0.0287), with equal GDS and LLC; S7/180 has better NHR (-0.238) but lower IWR (0.450) and worse LFR (-0.0264), again with equal GDS and LLC. Both compete for essentially the same space, so their future poses may change. S16/0 is most level (NHR -0.0145), with GDS 1 and LLC 0.517, but its IWR 0.238 and LFR -0.0669 are worse and its narrow footprint fills less of this opening. S6/0 fits farther right and has good IWR 0.582, GDS 1 and LLC 0.517, but NHR -0.667, LFR -0.0462 and its very thin shape make it a less substantial fill; saving it may preserve a useful small-gap option. S17/0 also uses the right side, but has poor NHR -0.889, IWR 0.240 and LFR -0.0974 despite GDS 1 and LLC 0.517.

S18 is the biggest future risk: its horizontal option has excellent IWR 1.083 but GDS 0, NHR -1.585, LLC 0.345 and LFR -0.095; its upright options have GDS 0 and LFR about -0.27 despite LLC 0.517. Placing S14 leaves S18, S15, S7, S16, S17 and S6 for later, but their future feasibility and final-wall metrics are unknown; no stone is unplaceable now, and no placement guarantees they remain placeable.

arguments.rationale:
S16 at 0° has the best course-height score (-0.058), full GDS (1.0), the strongest IWR among the full-GDS choices (0.605), tied-best LLC (0.517), and a fairly small local-void penalty (-0.048). Its tall, narrow shape may restrict later poses, but it uses the low right-hand area while leaving the thin S6 and wider S17 available; their future feasibility is not guaranteed.

S6 at 0° is denser and more flush (GDS 1, LFR -0.030), with good IWR (0.582) and the same LLC, but its NHR is worse (-0.667) and its very thin shape may be useful later. S6 at 180° is even more flush (-0.026) and has better NHR (-0.556), but weaker IWR (0.357). S17 at 0° is wide and fairly flush (LFR -0.035), with GDS 1 and LLC 0.517, but has worse NHR (-0.741) and IWR (0.5). S15 at 90° also fills the right side with GDS 1 and LLC 0.517, but has poorer NHR (-0.325), IWR (0.454), and LFR (-0.111). S17 at 270° has similar NHR and IWR to S15, slightly lower GDS (0.996), and worse LFR (-0.136).

The upper placements leave the right-hand options open but add height: S7 at 0° has GDS 0, NHR -1, IWR 0.366, LLC 0.517 and LFR -0.135. S18 at 180° has the best IWR (1.083) and spans widely, but GDS 0, NHR -1.585, LLC 0.345 and LFR -0.095. S17 and S7 at 180° have better IWR (0.725 and 0.732) and relatively modest void penalties (-0.040 and -0.047), but GDS 0, poor NHR (-2.148 and -1.738), and LLC 0.345. All six stones are currently placeable; none of these comparisons establishes their eventual placement or the final wall metrics.
